Location: Gore Road Trail, Fletcher Creek Ecological Preserve, Concession Road 7, Puslinch, ON, Canada
Remarks: Sunny 19-24C. Breezy at times.Walked up from Gore Rd, around the 2 shallow ponds, a short way up the grassy road towards the main lot. Daisies, purple vetch, birdsfoot trefoil. Milkweed beaking bud.
Comment: These are two different butterflies. The first perched one was beside the trail just inside the locked gate at Gore Rd. It was much smaller and paler than a nearby Pearly Eye. The upper dots seem the same size, the white rings around the lower eyes seem distinct not a cloud. The antenna were all orange at the tip with no black. I was looking for Eyed Browns the entire trip without success amongst the dozens of fast-flying Little Wood Satyrs. These 2 butterflies are the only ones that seemed different. The flying one is too out of focus to id but seems to lack spots on the upper wing. Possibly Appalachians?

Comment: Les plates-bandes derrière la maison font, cumulée, 20 m X 1 m. Depuis quelques années, nous laissons les Asclépiades communes y pousser, au profit des Monarques. Nous avons compté 23 chenilles dans la première plate-bande et 29 dans la deuxième. Devant la maison, près de la rue, il y a aussi quelques Asclépiades communes. Nous y avons vu une seule chenille. Un Monarque adulte a été vu près des plates-bandes vers midi le même jour. Au moins deux individus rôdent dans les environs des plates-bandes depuis début juillet.

Location: Between Knoll Path Ends, Rattray Marsh Conservation Area, Mississauga, ON, Canada
Remarks: Other butterflies seen on the walk are reported separately. Sunny. Warm 24C. Dry. Boneset, Goldenrods, Groundnut, Angelica, Queen Anne's Lace, Hog Peanut in bloom.
Comment: This butterfly appeared to be defending a territory on the inland side of the trail that connects the two ends of the Knoll Path, near the boardwalk that ends at Bexhill Road. It perched for long periods of time 4-8 feet off the ground. It went up after a Monarch and also a bee, chasing them aggressively. It also patrolled along the vegetation for short bursts from time to time. It was still there when I left and returned a half hour later. The photos are poor because I was on the trail trying to get an angle at a height above me and/or through vegetation. There is heavy use of this trail by families and pets.

Found in an open field dominated by Trifolium pratense near a slightly wooded area. Found alongside vegetation suited for habitats with poor water drainage/waterlogged soils (i.e. Populus deltoides).
Up to this point, have not seen any other Monarchs apart from the one previously recorded.  The butterfly was flying in a westerly direction.

Found in open fields between a lake and a wooded area. These fields were dominated by grasses or Trifolium pratense. The butterflies were often seen travelling back and forth between the open fields and the borders of the wooded areas (which were dominated by wetland species such as Equisetum arvense or Phragmites).

Cannot confirm ID for all the butterflies as some got away before I could assess the underside of their wings. Most likely still part of the Polyommatinae subfamily due to their size, wing shape and colour.
